Scrap is outside Section 232.

overview.intro:
Chapter 76 covers aluminum: unwrought metal (ingot, billet, slab, 7601), waste and scrap (7602), powders (7603), the mill products made from it (bars, rods and extruded profiles, wire, plate, sheet and strip, foil, tubes and fittings, 7604–7609), and articles of aluminum such as structures, doors and windows, cans and containers, gas cylinders, stranded cable, cookware and other articles (7610–7616). The base rates are low: **Free to 6.5%**, and Free for USMCA, KORUS and most other FTA partners.

What decides the cost is **Section 232**. Since April 6, 2026 it is charged on the **full customs value** (Proclamation 11021): **50%** on 92 lines, all the aluminum mill products and most articles (heading 9903.82.02), and **25%** on 15 derivative lines, household articles and cookware, sanitary ware, luggage frames, ladders and venetian blinds (9903.82.09). It applies to every country, and FTA or USMCA claims do not reduce it. UK aluminum that is at least 95% UK-smelted or cast pays half (25% or 15%). Chinese aluminum pays Section 301 on top (75% to 81% in total), Russian aluminum, or aluminum made from Russian-smelted metal, **200%**. Since September 15, 2026 Canadian bars, profiles and tubes (7604, 7608) also pay the **50% Section 338** duty, so **100%** in total.

Scrap, powders, tanks, most fasteners, pot scourers and wire cloth (17 lines) are **outside Section 232**. On top of the tariff, many aluminum products carry **antidumping and countervailing duties**: extrusions, foil, common alloy sheet, wire and cable, lithographic plates and disposable containers. They are company-specific and not part of this table or the calculator; see Tariff updates and Import documents.

productGroups.label: Unwrought aluminum (ingot, billet, slab)
productGroups.blurb: Primary and secondary aluminum ingot, T-bar, sow, billet, sheet ingot and foundry alloy: 13 lines, Free or 2.1%–2.6%. Section 232 50% (9903.82.02) from every country; the largest import group (≈$9.9B in 2025, mostly from Canada).

productGroups.label: Aluminum waste and scrap
productGroups.blurb: Used beverage cans, wheels, production scrap (turnings, clippings) and other scrap: 5 lines, all Free. Outside Section 232 and on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so Free except for China (25%), Brazil (25%) and Russia.

productGroups.label: Aluminum powders and flakes
productGroups.blurb: Non-lamellar and lamellar powders and flakes: 2 lines at 5% and 3.9%. Outside Section 232; pays the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%) for most countries.

productGroups.label: Aluminum bars, rods and profiles (extrusions)
productGroups.blurb: Extruded hollow and solid profiles, bars and rods: 13 lines, 1.5%–5%. Section 232 50%; Canadian goods also pay the 50% Section 338 duty (100% in total). Chinese extrusions are under AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Aluminum wire
productGroups.blurb: Unstranded wire of non-alloy or alloy aluminum, including wire rod over 7 mm: 4 lines, 2.6% or 4.2%. Section 232 50%.

productGroups.label: Aluminum plate, sheet and strip (over 0.2 mm)
productGroups.blurb: Plate, sheet and strip, rectangular or other, clad or not, including can body and lid stock: 19 lines, 2.7%–6.5%. Section 232 50%. Common alloy sheet from China and 16 other countries is under AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Aluminum foil (0.2 mm or less)
productGroups.blurb: Plain, rolled, etched capacitor, cut-to-shape and backed foil: 11 lines, Free–5.8%. Section 232 50%. Foil from China, Armenia, Brazil, Oman, Russia and Türkiye is under AD or CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Aluminum tubes and pipes
productGroups.blurb: Seamless and welded tubes and pipes: 4 lines at 5.7%. Section 232 50%; Canadian tubes also pay Section 338 (100% in total) unless for civil aircraft.

productGroups.label: Aluminum tube and pipe fittings
productGroups.blurb: Couplings, elbows, sleeves and other fittings: 1 line at 5.7%. Section 232 50%.

productGroups.label: Aluminum structures, doors and windows
productGroups.blurb: Doors, windows and frames, thresholds, roofing and siding, architectural work, mobile homes and other structures: 7 lines at 5.7%. Section 232 50% as derivative aluminum.

productGroups.label: Aluminum tanks and vats (over 300 liters)
productGroups.blurb: Reservoirs, tanks and vats over 300 liters, not fitted with machinery: 2 lines at 2.6%. Outside Section 232; pays the 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Aluminum cans, drums and containers (300 liters or less)
productGroups.blurb: Collapsible tubes, beverage and food cans, drums and other containers: 6 lines, Free–5.7%. Section 232 50% as derivative aluminum.

productGroups.label: Aluminum gas cylinders
productGroups.blurb: Containers for compressed or liquefied gas: 1 line at 5%. Section 232 50%; DOT specification rules for cylinders.

productGroups.label: Stranded aluminum wire and cable
productGroups.blurb: Stranded wire, cables and plaited bands, with or without steel core (ACSR): 6 lines, 4.9% or 5.7%. Section 232 50% as derivative aluminum. Chinese wire and cable is under AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Aluminum cookware, household articles and sanitary ware
productGroups.blurb: Cookware, bakeware, foil containers and other household articles, pot scourers and sanitary ware: 13 lines, 3.1% or 3.8%. Section 232 25% (9903.82.09) on 12 lines; pot scourers are outside. Chinese disposable foil containers are under AD/CVD orders.

productGroups.label: Other articles of aluminum
productGroups.blurb: Fasteners, wire cloth and fencing, luggage frames, ladders, venetian blinds, pipe hangers, castings, forgings and other articles: 17 lines, Free–6%. Section 232 50% on castings, forgings and most other articles, 25% on ladders, blinds and luggage frames; most fasteners and wire cloth are outside.

workedExamples.title: $1,000,000 of primary aluminum ingot from Canada
workedExamples.body: Unwrought aluminum of 99.9% or more is **Free**, but it is a Section 232 aluminum article, so it pays **+50% of its full value** (9903.82.02): **$500,000**, with or without a USMCA certification (note 16(b)). Canada lost its Section 232 exemption on March 12, 2025. A 25% rate (9903.82.19) exists only for limited quantities that Commerce authorizes for Canadian or Mexican producers that commit to new U.S. aluminum capacity.

workedExamples.title: Extruded hollow profiles from Canada
workedExamples.body: Base **1.5%**, Free under USMCA, plus **50%** Section 232 (9903.82.02), plus **50%** Section 338 (9903.03.14), which Proclamation 11065 extended to Canadian 7604 and 7608 goods and made cumulative with Section 232 from September 15, 2026. Total **100%** with a USMCA claim, **101.5%** without: $100,000 of extrusions owes $100,000.

workedExamples.title: Can body stock from South Korea
workedExamples.body: Base **3%**, Free under KORUS, but Section 232 adds **50%** on the full value (9903.82.02): **50%** in total. The 2026 Section 301 duty on Korea does not apply to Section 232 aluminum (note 52(f)(1)). Korea is not among the countries in the common alloy aluminum sheet AD/CVD orders.

workedExamples.title: Aluminum bakeware from China
workedExamples.body: Household articles of 7615 are derivative aluminum at the **25%** Section 232 rate (9903.82.09). This line also pays **7.5%** under Section 301 List 4A (9903.88.15) and its **3.1%** base rate: **35.6%**. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China does not apply to it. Disposable foil pans and containers (7615.10.71.25) from China are also under AD/CVD orders.

workedExamples.title: Used beverage can scrap from Mexico
workedExamples.body: Aluminum scrap is **Free**, is not a Section 232 article, and is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (9903.05.86), so Mexican or Canadian UBC scrap pays **no duty**. Chinese scrap pays 25% (Section 301 List 3) and Brazilian scrap 25% (9903.05.01).

workedExamples.title: Aluminum billet from the United Arab Emirates
workedExamples.body: Alloy billet is **Free**, plus **50%** Section 232 (9903.82.02): $50,000 on $100,000. The UAE is one of the 60 economies of the 2026 Section 301 actions (12.5%), but that duty does not apply to Section 232 aluminum. If any primary aluminum in the billet was smelted in Russia, it pays **200%** instead (9903.85.67).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Subheading note 1.** (a) *Aluminum, not alloyed*: metal containing by weight at least 99% aluminum, with iron plus silicon not over 1% and each other element (for example Cr, Cu, Mg, Mn, Ni, Zn) not over 0.1% (copper up to 0.2% if chromium and manganese are each not over 0.05%). (b) *Aluminum alloys*: metallic substances in which aluminum predominates by weight over each other element, provided at least one other element (or iron plus silicon) exceeds those limits, or the other elements together exceed 1%.

**Subheading note 2.** For subheading 7616.91, *wire* means products of any cross-sectional shape with no cross-sectional dimension over 6 mm (notwithstanding note 9(c) to Section XV).

seo.title: Aluminum Tariff Updates 2025–2026: 50% Section 232, Full-Value Rule, Canada, UK, Russia (HTS Ch. 76) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every U.S. aluminum tariff change since 2025 with Federal Register citations: Section 232 raised to 25% (March 2025) and 50% (June 2025), rebuilt on full value (April 2026), Canada Section 338 on extrusions and tubes, the UK rate, Russia 200%, the end of the IEEPA duties, and aluminum AD/CVD orders.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 76 today. Base rates did not change; only 8 statistical lines were added or renumbered (pure aluminum ingot, scrap and small cans).

The extra duties changed a lot. In January 2025 aluminum paid **10%** under Section 232, with Canada, Mexico and Australia exempt and Argentina, the EU and the UK under quotas. Proclamation 10895 raised it to **25%** and ended those arrangements on **March 12, 2025**; Proclamation 10947 raised it to **50% on June 4, 2025** (UK 25%); and Proclamation 11021 rebuilt it on **April 6, 2026** on the **full customs value**: 50% on aluminum articles and most derivatives (9903.82.02), 25% on household articles, ladders, blinds and luggage frames (9903.82.09). Russian aluminum has paid **200%** since 2023. On **September 15, 2026** the Canada Section 338 duty (50%) was extended to Canadian extrusions and tubes and made cumulative with Section 232.

The IEEPA duties ended on **February 24, 2026** and the Section 122 surcharge on July 23, 2026; neither added to Section 232 aluminum. The 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties also leave Section 232 aluminum alone, while China's Section 301 duty stacks. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders are listed for reference and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 76 from any country: Section 232 aluminum (note 16) and the Russia 200% (note 19), China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50, 52), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA and Section 122 duties. The main antidumping and countervailing duty orders on Chapter 76 products are listed for reference; the calculator does not model them. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.country: All countries (Canada, Mexico, UAE, EU, Korea, India and Bahrain included)

inEffect.before: +10% (9903.85.01), with Canada, Mexico and Australia exempt and Argentina, the EU and the UK under quotas
inEffect.exemption: Covers 107 of 124 lines. 50% (9903.82.02, note 16(c)(i)–(ii)): all of 7601 and 7604–7609, structures (7610), cans and containers (7612), gas cylinders (7613), stranded wire (7614), castings, forgings and most other articles of 7616. 25% (9903.82.09, note 16(c)(vi)): household articles and cookware, sanitary ware (7615.10.20–7615.20), luggage frames, ladders and venetian blinds. Not covered: scrap (7602), powders (7603), tanks (7611), pot scourers (7615.10.11), fasteners other than 7616.10.90.90, and wire cloth (7616.91). No country exemptions, quotas or product exclusions (ended March 12, 2025; the inclusions process ended April 6, 2026). Note 16(b): collected on top of any FTA or USMCA rate. Lower rates: UK with ≥95% UK-smelted or cast aluminum (9903.82.04, 25%; 9903.82.05, 15%), derivatives with ≥85% U.S.-smelted and cast aluminum (9903.82.06, 10%), and Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican quantities (9903.82.19, 25%). Goods under these headings do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Aluminum mill products pay half their value again in duty: $400,000 of sheet, foil, extrusions or ingot from any country owes $200,000, whatever the FTA claim; cookware and ladders pay a quarter.

inEffect.before: Tariff-rate quota: Free in quota, +10% over quota (Proclamation 10405)
inEffect.now: +25% (derivatives +15%) with ≥95% UK-smelted or cast aluminum; otherwise +50% / +25%
inEffect.exemption: Note 16(d): the lower UK rates apply only when at least 95% of the aluminum was smelted or most recently cast in the United Kingdom. Executive Order 14309 contemplates further arrangements for UK metals, but no quota has been set up. UK aluminum that does not meet the test pays the standard 50% or 25%. The 10% 2026 Section 301 duty on the UK (9903.05.81) applies only to the 12 non-Section 232 lines.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A UK rolling mill using UK-cast metal ships sheet at half the duty of every other country: $100,000 of UK sheet pays $25,000 plus its base rate.

inEffect.country: Russia, and aluminum made with Russian-smelted or Russian-cast metal from any country
inEffect.measure: Section 232 aluminum (Russia) + rates in lieu of column 2

inEffect.now: +200% on 110 lines, on top of the column 2 rate or 70% in its place; +12.5% Section 301
inEffect.exemption: Note 19(m): 200% on aluminum articles (9903.85.67, 73 lines) and derivative aluminum articles (9903.85.68, 37 lines) that are products of Russia, or of any country when any amount of the primary aluminum was smelted in Russia or the article was cast in Russia (Proclamation 10522). Russia pays column 2 rates, or 70% in their place on the note 30(d) subheadings (9903.90.09, 54 Chapter 76 lines, Proclamation 10523). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on Russia (9903.05.66) stacks on the 200%. The calculator applies the 200% to products of Russia only; it cannot test smelt or cast country.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian aluminum, or Turkish or Indian sheet made from Russian-smelted ingot, is priced out of the U.S. market: $100,000 owes more than $200,000.

inEffect.now: +50% on bars, rods and profiles (7604) and tubes and pipes (7608), on top of Section 232: 100%
inEffect.exemption: Proclamation 11065 added 7604 and 7608 to the note 51(b)(3) list and made the duty cumulative with Section 232 from September 15, 2026. Charged even when USMCA is claimed (the heading's Special column is "+ 50%"). Canadian tubes and pipes for civil aircraft that meet general note 6 are exempt (9903.03.16). Other Canadian Chapter 76 goods pay Section 232 only; the 10% 2026 Section 301 duty on Canada (9903.05.29) is lifted for USMCA goods (9903.05.93) and does not apply to Section 232 aluminum.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian extrusions and tubes cost twice their value in duty: $250,000 of profiles owes $250,000, USMCA or not.

inEffect.exemption: Note 31 (9903.91.01, 25%) covers 62 lines, the unwrought aluminum and mill products of 7601 and 7604–7609, since September 27, 2024; List 3 (9903.88.03, 25%) covers scrap, powders, structures, cans, cylinders, sanitary ware and most of 7616 (41 lines); List 2 (9903.88.02, 25%) 3 stranded conductor lines; List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%) etched capacitor, cut-to-shape and backed foil, doors and windows, and most cookware (12 lines). These stack with Section 232. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China (9903.05.31) applies only to the 12 non-Section 232 lines outside the note 52(b) exemption list. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue during the four-year review.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese ingot, sheet, foil and extrusions pay 75% to 81% of their value; Chinese cookware 28% to 36%; Chinese scrap 25%.

inEffect.country: 60 Section 301 economies (Canada, Mexico, UAE, Korea, India, Bahrain, Colombia, EU, Thailand, UK, Japan, Taiwan, Vietnam and others)

inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 aluminum (note 52(f)(1)), and scrap (7602) is on the general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86). It charges the 12 other lines: powders (7603), tanks (7611), pot scourers (7615.10.11), fasteners other than 7616.10.90.90, and wire cloth (7616.91). USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Only a few non-Section 232 goods pay it: $100,000 of Indian aluminum rivets (7616.10.30, 4.7%) pays $14,700.

inEffect.now: +25% on the 17 non-Section 232 lines (plus 12.5% on 12 of them)
inEffect.exemption: Does not apply to Section 232 aluminum (note 50(a)(vi)(1)), so Brazilian sheet, foil and ingot pay only Section 232. It charges scrap, powders, tanks, pot scourers, most fasteners and wire cloth. Brazilian foil and common alloy sheet are also under AD orders.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian aluminum scrap pays 25%; Brazilian powder pays 5% + 25% + 12.5% = 42.5%.

changes.title: No Chapter 76 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 116 of 124 Chapter 76 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; the 8 others are new statistical lines at unchanged rates. Pure unwrought aluminum 7601.10.60.30 was split into 7601.10.60.40 (99.9% or more) and 7601.10.60.45 (over 99.8% but under 99.9%); scrap 7602.00.00 was renumbered, adding recyclable auto and truck wheels (.45), industrial scrap (.55), other recyclable aluminum (.65) and other (.75); and small cans 7612.90.10.30 were split by cross-section (.40, .45).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), on every Chapter 76 line. Note 29 has no Section 232 carve-out, so it will add to the 50% on Nicaraguan aluminum. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Circumvention inquiry: Chinese aluminum composite panels
changes.detail: Commerce self-initiated an inquiry into whether aluminum composite panels made in China by Shanghai Alumetal Decorative Material Co. circumvent the AD/CVD orders on common alloy aluminum sheet from China. If affirmative, those panels pay the sheet cash deposits.

changes.title: Five-year reviews of the aluminum foil orders
changes.detail: The ITC instituted the first five-year reviews of the antidumping duty orders on aluminum foil from Armenia, Brazil, Oman, Russia and Türkiye and the countervailing duty orders on Oman and Türkiye (in place since 2021). The orders stay in force during the reviews.

changes.title: Common alloy sheet orders revoked for certain can stock
changes.detail: After changed circumstances reviews, Commerce revoked the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on common alloy aluminum sheet from China and 16 other countries in part, for certain aluminum can stock. The rest of the orders continue (Commerce found in July 2026 sunset reviews that revoking them would likely lead to continued dumping and subsidies; the ITC is conducting full reviews).
changes.countries: China, Bahrain, Brazil, Croatia, Egypt, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Oman, Romania, Serbia, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, Taiwan, Türkiye

changes.title: Section 338 duty reaches Canadian extrusions and tubes, on top of Section 232
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added aluminum bars, rods and profiles (7604) and tubes and pipes (7608) to the note 51(b)(3) list of the 50% Section 338 duty on products of Canada (9903.03.14), and from September 15, 2026 the duty applies in addition to Section 232. With USMCA these goods now pay 100%; without it, their base rate on top. Tubes for civil aircraft meeting general note 6 are exempt (9903.03.16). The duty started August 22, 2026 under Proclamation 11048 (delayed by Proclamation 11056) but did not reach Chapter 76 until this change.

changes.title: Circumvention inquiries: aluminum containers from Indonesia and Malaysia
changes.detail: Commerce opened country-wide inquiries into whether disposable aluminum containers, pans, trays and lids completed in Indonesia and Malaysia from Chinese aluminum foil circumvent the 2025 AD/CVD orders on China (7615.10.71.25).

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: Section 232 aluminum exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect. They do not apply to Section 232 aluminum (note 52(f)(1)), and scrap is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). In Chapter 76 they charge 12 lines: powders, tanks, pot scourers, most fasteners and wire cloth. USMCA goods are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It did not apply in addition to Section 232 duties (Proclamation 11012), so Section 232 aluminum paid only its 50% or 25%; the non-Section 232 lines paid it unless USMCA goods or on its product exemption list (9903.03.03).

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil: Section 232 aluminum exempt, scrap not
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect. Section 232 aluminum is excluded (note 50(a)(vi)(1)), so it reaches the 17 other Chapter 76 lines: scrap, powders, tanks, pot scourers, most fasteners and wire cloth.

changes.title: Half-rate import quota for companies building U.S. primary aluminum capacity
changes.detail: Proclamation 11045 directs Commerce to approve onshoring plans of companies that commit to build, refurbish or expand a U.S. primary aluminum smelter (construction to start by January 20, 2029). Approved companies may import each year a quantity of primary aluminum matching the project's expected annual output at half the Section 232 rate (25%). No Federal Register procedures or HTS heading had been published as of October 12, 2026.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032 adjusts the metals program
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, aluminum content counts as U.S.-smelted and cast for the 10% derivative rate (9903.82.06) when at least 85% by weight was smelted and cast in the United States, and new rates apply to HVAC, agricultural, industrial and mobile equipment derivatives. Chapter 76 aluminum articles stay at 50% (UK 25%).

changes.title: Commerce corrects the Section 232 annexes
changes.detail: Commerce published technical corrections to the HTS for Proclamation 11021, including heading 9903.82.01 (articles on the lists that contain no aluminum, steel or copper pay no Section 232 duty) from April 6, 2026. Chapter 76 articles are made of aluminum, so it rarely applies to them.

changes.title: Commerce opens the 25% route for Canadian and Mexican aluminum producers
changes.detail: Commerce set out how aluminum and steel producers with plants in Canada or Mexico that supply U.S. vehicle makers can apply for a tariff cut of up to half (not below 25%), limited to quantities equal to newly committed U.S. primary aluminum or steel capacity. Approved aluminum enters under 9903.82.19 (+25%, note 16(i)).

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum rebuilt on full value (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier aluminum headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value regardless of metal content. In Chapter 76, aluminum articles and most derivatives stay at 50% (9903.82.02, 92 lines) and household articles, sanitary ware, luggage frames, ladders and venetian blinds pay 25% (9903.82.09, 15 lines). UK products need at least 95% UK-smelted or cast aluminum for 25% / 15% (9903.82.04 / .05); derivatives made with U.S.-smelted aluminum pay 10% (9903.82.06). The derivatives inclusions process ended, goods entering a foreign-trade zone must take privileged foreign status, and manufacturing drawback is allowed only under clause 13.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs; Section 232 aluminum outside it
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Proclamation 11012 says it does not apply in addition to Section 232 duties, so Section 232 aluminum paid only its Section 232 rate; USMCA goods were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24, 2026. Section 232 aluminum duties are not IEEPA duties and continued unchanged.

changes.title: Authority to halve Section 232 for some Canadian and Mexican aluminum
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 (medium- and heavy-duty vehicles) authorized Commerce to cut the Section 232 aluminum and steel duty by up to half, but not below 25%, for limited quantities from Canadian or Mexican producers that supply U.S. vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. capacity.

changes.title: Aluminum wire and cable orders on China continued
changes.detail: After sunset reviews, Commerce continued the 2019 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum wire and cable from China (mainly 7614 and 8544).

changes.title: UK Economic Prosperity Deal: UK aluminum stays at 25%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14309, implementing the U.S.-UK Economic Prosperity Deal, kept UK aluminum and steel at 25% and contemplated further arrangements once the UK meets U.S. supply-chain requirements. None has been set up; since April 6, 2026 the UK rate requires at least 95% UK-smelted or cast aluminum.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum tariff doubled to 50%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 aluminum and steel duties from 25% to 50% for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4, 2025, except for the UK (25%). It also said that Section 232 aluminum no longer paid the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on Chinese disposable aluminum containers
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on disposable aluminum containers, pans, trays and lids from China (7615.10.71.25).

changes.title: Non-stacking order: Canada and Mexico IEEPA duty in place of Section 232
changes.detail: Executive Order 14289, retroactive to March 4, 2025, said goods of Canada and Mexico subject to the IEEPA duties would not also pay the Section 232 aluminum duty. Proclamation 10947 reversed the order of precedence from June 4, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff excludes Section 232 aluminum
changes.detail: Executive Order 14257 set the reciprocal tariffs from April 5, 2025 but excluded aluminum articles and derivatives subject to Section 232 (Annex II). Non-Section 232 Chapter 76 lines such as scrap paid it unless exempted. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum raised to 25%; all exemptions and quotas end
changes.detail: Proclamation 10895 raised the Section 232 aluminum duty from 10% to 25% and ended the exemptions of Canada, Mexico and Australia and the arrangements with Argentina, the EU and the UK, and stopped new product exclusions, from March 12, 2025. It also added derivative aluminum articles and set up an inclusions process (ended April 6, 2026).

changes.title: IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA goods were exempted from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on aluminum lithographic printing plates
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping duty orders on aluminum lithographic printing plates from China and Japan and a countervailing duty order on China. In March 2026 the ITC began remand proceedings on its injury determinations after a court order; the orders remain in place pending the outcome.

changes.title: China Section 301: aluminum products to 25%

changes.title: Mexico: 10% on aluminum smelted or cast in China, Russia, Belarus or Iran
changes.detail: Proclamation 10782 charged the 10% Section 232 duty on Mexican aluminum that contained primary aluminum smelted, or was cast, in China, Russia, Belarus or Iran, while other Mexican aluminum stayed exempt. Superseded on March 12, 2025, when all Mexican aluminum became dutiable.

changes.title: Aluminum foil orders on China continued

changes.title: Russian aluminum: 200%

Proclamation 10895 restated it under note 19(m) from March 12, 2025 (9903.85.67, 9903.85.68).

changes.title: Aluminum extrusions orders on China continued

changes.title: UK aluminum tariff-rate quota
changes.detail: Proclamation 10405 let UK aluminum enter free of Section 232 duty within an annual quota, with 10% above it, from June 1, 2022. Ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: EU aluminum tariff-rate quota
changes.detail: Proclamation 10327 set a duty-free quota for EU aluminum smelted and cast in the EU from January 1, 2022. Ended March 12, 2025.

changes.title: AD orders on aluminum foil from five countries

changes.title: First aluminum derivatives: stranded wire and auto parts
changes.detail: Proclamation 9980 extended the 10% Section 232 aluminum duty to certain derivative articles, including stranded wire and cable (7614) and aluminum bumper and body stampings for vehicles, from February 8, 2020.

changes.title: Canada and Mexico exempted from Section 232 aluminum
changes.detail: Proclamation 9893 removed the Section 232 aluminum duty on Canada and Mexico from May 20, 2019. The exemption lasted until March 12, 2025.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum tariff begins at 10%

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 76 aluminum were **$26.47B in 2025**, -6.5% from $28.31B in 2024 (peak: $36.66B in 2022). The five largest suppliers were Canada ($9.69B, 37%), China ($1.97B), Mexico ($1.81B), the United Arab Emirates ($1.61B) and South Korea ($1.23B). By product group the largest were unwrought aluminum (7601, $9.94B), plate, sheet and strip (7606, $3.83B), structures, doors and windows (7610, $2.24B) and scrap (7602, $2.16B).

2025 was the year Section 232 changed most: Canada, Mexico and Australia lost their exemptions and the rate went from 10% to 25% on March 12 and to 50% on June 4. Imports from Canada fell 15.6% and from China 35.9%, while the UAE (+25.6%), Korea (+25.5%), India (+22.5%) and Thailand (+23.5%) grew. Scrap, outside Section 232, rose 61.7% to $2.16B.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

seo.shortDescription: The total U.S. tariff on aluminum by country and product: 50% on ingot, sheet and foil from Canada, Mexico, the UAE, Korea, India, Bahrain and the EU; 100% on Canadian extrusions and tubes; China 75%+; UK 25% with UK-smelted metal; Russia 200%+. industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. For aluminum mill products (7601, 7604–7609) and most articles the answer is almost the same everywhere: **50% plus the base rate**, or **50%** for FTA partners whose base rate is Free, because Section 232 has no country exemptions and is collected on top of FTA and USMCA rates. Cookware, sanitary ware, ladders, blinds and luggage frames pay **25%**. China pays **75% to 81%**, Canadian extrusions and tubes **100%** (Section 338), and UK aluminum with at least 95% UK-smelted or cast metal half the standard rate (the cells show the default).

Scrap (7602) is Free for almost everyone. Powders, tanks, pot scourers, most fasteners and wire cloth are outside Section 232 and pay their base rate plus, for most countries, the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%). The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties, which apply company by company to extrusions, foil, common alloy sheet, wire and cable, lithographic plates and disposable containers (see Tariff updates).

rule.label: 50% on aluminum articles, with or without a USMCA claim: Section 232 (9903.82.02) has had no Canada exemption since March 12, 2025 and is collected on top of the USMCA rate (note 16(b)); 25% on cookware, ladders and blinds (9903.82.09). Bars, rods, profiles (7604) and tubes (7608) also pay 50% under Section 338 (9903.03.14) since September 15, 2026: 100% (civil-aircraft tubes exempt). Commerce can authorize limited quantities at 25% (9903.82.19). Scrap is Free; 12 non-Section 232 lines pay 10% under Section 301 (9903.05.29) unless USMCA is claimed.

industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2(aa), 16, 19, 20, 29, 30, 31, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 16(c) lists 92 Chapter 76 lines at 50% (aluminum articles and derivatives, (i)–(ii)) and 15 at 25% (derivatives, (vi)); scrap, powders, tanks, pot scourers, most fasteners and wire cloth are on no list. There is no country exemption, and note 16(b) collects the duty on top of FTA rates. Section 232 aluminum is excluded from the 2026 Section 301 duties (note 52(f)(1)), the Brazil duty (note 50(a)(vi)(1)) and the expired Section 122 surcharge, but not from China Section 301 (notes 20, 31), the Russia 200% (note 19(m)) or the 2027 Nicaragua duty (note 29). Scrap (7602) is on the 2026 Section 301 general exemption list (note 52(b)); 7604 and 7608 are on the Canada Section 338 list (note 51(b)(3)), with a civil-aircraft exemption (note 51(d)) for 7608.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 76: Aluminum and Articles Thereof — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Aluminum: AIM License, Smelt-and-Cast Country, Section 232 Entry Rules & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 76) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 76 aluminum line: Commerce aluminum import license (AIM), country of smelt and cast, the Russia 200% rule, Section 232 entry (9903.82.02 / .09), FTZ status, AD/CVD scope, plus the legal ways to pay less: UK-smelted metal, U.S.-smelted content, the Canada/Mexico 25% route, correct classification and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
For aluminum, the paperwork is part of the duty. Most entries of basic aluminum products need a **Commerce aluminum import license (AIM)** that names the countries where the primary aluminum was **smelted** and where the product was most recently **cast**. Those answers decide whether the shipment pays 50% or **200%** (any Russian-smelted or Russian-cast metal), and whether UK or U.S.-metal rates apply. The Section 232 heading (9903.82.02 or 9903.82.09, or a reduced-rate heading) is reported next to the Chapter 76 line, and the duty is charged on the full value with no FTA reduction.

The legal ways to pay less are narrow: product exclusions and country quotas are gone. What remains: UK-smelted or cast aluminum (25% / 15%), derivatives made with U.S.-smelted aluminum (10%), Commerce-authorized Canadian or Mexican quantities (25%), avoiding Chinese origin (Section 301), classifying correctly, checking AD/CVD scope before you buy, and limited drawback. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Buy UK aluminum smelted or cast in the UK
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty: 25% (9903.82.04) instead of 50%, or 15% (9903.82.05) instead of 25% on derivatives
levers.appliesTo: Section 232 lines (107 of 124) of the United Kingdom
levers.document: Mill certificates and the AIM license showing the country of smelt and cast; at least 95% of the aluminum must be smelted or most recently cast in the UK (note 16(d)).
levers.caveat: Origin must be the UK and the 95% test must be met; otherwise 50% or 25%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(d), headings 9903.82.04–.05

levers.title: Derivatives made with U.S.-smelted aluminum: 10%
levers.appliesTo: The 40 derivative aluminum lines: structures, doors and windows (7610), cans (7612), cylinders (7613), stranded wire (7614), household articles (7615) and parts of 7616
levers.document: Proof that at least 85% by weight of the aluminum content was smelted and cast in the United States (supplier certificates, AIM data), declared at entry under 9903.82.06.
levers.caveat: Not for aluminum articles of 7601 and 7604–7609. The 85% threshold applies from June 8, 2026 (Proclamation 11032).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(e), heading 9903.82.06

levers.title: Canada or Mexico: the Commerce-authorized 25% rate
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 duty (25% instead of 50%) on authorized quantities
levers.appliesTo: Aluminum articles of Canada or Mexico (note 16(c)(i)) that qualify for USMCA
levers.document: Commerce authorization for the producer (submission under the April 23, 2026 procedures), USMCA certification of origin, and entry under heading 9903.82.19.
levers.caveat: Only for producers that supply U.S. vehicle makers and commit to new U.S. primary aluminum capacity, and only for the quantity Commerce sets. Canadian 7604 and 7608 goods still pay the Section 338 duty.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(i), heading 9903.82.19

levers.title: Build U.S. smelting capacity: half-rate primary aluminum quota
levers.saves: Half the Section 232 rate (25%) on a yearly quantity of primary aluminum equal to the new project's expected output
levers.appliesTo: Primary unwrought aluminum (7601) imported by companies with a Commerce-approved onshoring plan
levers.document: An onshoring plan approved by Commerce committing to build, refurbish or expand a U.S. primary aluminum facility, with construction starting by January 20, 2029.
levers.caveat: Signed July 20, 2026; Commerce had not published procedures or an HTS heading as of October 12, 2026. Benefits can be rescinded, retroactively in case of fraud.

levers.title: Avoid Chinese origin and Russian metal
levers.saves: 25% of value on Chinese aluminum (Section 301 on top of Section 232); 150 points or more by avoiding Russian-smelted or Russian-cast metal (200% instead of 50%)
levers.document: Mill certificates and the AIM license naming the smelt and cast countries. Tariff origin follows the last substantial transformation (for Chapter 76, the rules of 19 CFR 102.20); ask CBP for a binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Third-country processing does not change the Section 232 rate and can fall under AD/CVD circumvention findings: Commerce is investigating Chinese foil turned into containers in Indonesia and Malaysia. The 200% applies whatever the country of origin if any primary aluminum was smelted in Russia.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 19(m) and 31

levers.title: Classify correctly
levers.saves: The Section 232 duty on lines that are on no note 16(c) list (scrap, powders, tanks, most fasteners, wire cloth), or the 25-point gap between 50% and 25% derivatives
levers.document: Technical specifications (scrap vs remelt ingot under statistical note 5; fastener type; household article vs other article) and, if unsure, a CBP binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Classification follows the product, not the duty: misclassifying ingot as scrap or a part as a fastener is a penalty case.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16(c)

levers.title: Claim USMCA for the non-Section 232 lines
levers.saves: The base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty on Canadian and Mexican powders, tanks, pot scourers, fasteners and wire cloth (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94)
levers.appliesTo: The 12 Chapter 76 lines that pay the 2026 Section 301 duty, for originating goods of Canada or Mexico
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer (no set format), available to CBP on request.
levers.caveat: A USMCA claim does not reduce Section 232 (note 16(b)) or the Section 338 duty on Canadian extrusions and tubes.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52

levers.title: Canadian tubes for civil aircraft
levers.saves: The 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian tubes and pipes (9903.03.16)
levers.appliesTo: Tubes and pipes of 7608 of Canada for civil aircraft
levers.document: Proof that the goods meet general note 6 (civil aircraft), as for a "C" claim.
levers.caveat: Section 232 (50%) still applies. No such relief exists for Canadian extrusions of 7604.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 51(d), heading 9903.03.16

levers.title: Check AD/CVD scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping or countervailing duty, when the product or producer is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: Extrusions (7604, 7608, 7610, 7616), common alloy sheet (7606), foil (7607), wire and cable (7605, 7614), lithographic plates and disposable containers (7615)
levers.document: The order's written scope (it, not the HTS number, decides) and the producer's company-specific cash-deposit rate; when unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.
levers.caveat: A product in scope pays the cash deposit even if entered under another HTS line. Certain can stock was removed from the common alloy sheet orders in September 2026.

citations.label: Common alloy sheet: can stock revocation (91 FR 60591)

levers.title: Drawback: limited for Section 232

seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. aluminum tariffs: the current rate, whether the 50% aluminum tariff is still in effect, aluminum tariffs on Canada, Mexico, China, the UK and the EU, scrap, cookware, exemptions, how the duty is calculated, and HS codes for aluminum.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on aluminum imports, by country, by product and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Aluminum ingot and mill products (HTS 7601, 7604–7609) and most aluminum articles pay the Section 232 duty of 50% of their full customs value, from every country and on top of any FTA or USMCA rate; cookware, sanitary ware, ladders, blinds and luggage frames pay 25%. UK aluminum with at least 95% UK-smelted or cast metal pays half.

Chinese aluminum pays 75% to 81% (Section 232 + Section 301). Canadian extrusions and tubes pay 100% since September 15, 2026 (Section 232 + Section 338). Aluminum containing any Russian-smelted or Russian-cast metal pays 200%.

Scrap, powders, tanks, most fasteners and wire cloth are outside Section 232; scrap is Free for almost every country. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and never added to Section 232 aluminum after June 2025. AD/CVD on extrusions, foil, sheet, wire and cable and containers come on top.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $26.47B of Chapter 76 aluminum, Canada ($9.69B, 37%) first, then China ($1.97B), Mexico ($1.81B) and the UAE ($1.61B).

faqs.question: What is the current U.S. tariff on aluminum?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on aluminum right now
is there a tariff on aluminum
faqs.answer: 50% of the full customs value for aluminum ingot, bars, profiles, wire, sheet, foil, tubes and fittings (HTS 7601, 7604–7609) and most aluminum articles, from every country, under Section 232 heading 9903.82.02, on top of the base rate (Free to 6.5%). Cookware, sanitary ware, ladders, venetian blinds and luggage frames pay 25% (9903.82.09). UK aluminum at least 95% smelted or cast in the UK pays 25% (or 15%). China pays another 25% or 7.5% under Section 301, and aluminum with Russian-smelted or cast metal 200%. Scrap and a few other lines are not covered.

faqs.question: Is the 50% aluminum tariff still in effect, and when did it start?
searchedAs: is the 50 aluminum tariff still in effect
are aluminum tariffs still in effect
faqs.answer: Yes. Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 aluminum duty from 25% to 50% for goods entered from 12:01 a.m. EDT on June 4, 2025. Proclamation 11021 kept 50% when it moved the duty to heading 9903.82.02 on the full customs value from April 6, 2026, and it is in the current tariff schedule (2026 Revision 21). The Supreme Court's February 20, 2026 ruling in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump ended only the IEEPA tariffs; the aluminum tariff rests on Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 and was not affected.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on aluminum from Canada?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on aluminum from canada
faqs.answer: 50% on Canadian aluminum ingot, sheet, foil, wire and most articles, with or without a USMCA claim: Canada's Section 232 exemption ended March 12, 2025, and note 16(b) collects the duty on top of the USMCA rate. Canadian bars, rods, profiles (7604) and tubes (7608) also pay the 50% Section 338 duty since September 15, 2026: 100% in total (tubes for civil aircraft exempt from Section 338). Commerce can authorize limited quantities at 25% (9903.82.19). Canadian scrap is Free. Canada shipped $9.69B in 2025, 37% of U.S. aluminum imports.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on aluminum from Mexico?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on aluminum from mexico
is there a tariff on aluminum from mexico
faqs.answer: 50% on Mexican aluminum articles (Section 232, 9903.82.02), and 25% on cookware, ladders and blinds, even with a USMCA certification. Mexico's exemption, and the 2024 rule that charged 10% on Mexican aluminum made with Chinese, Russian, Belarusian or Iranian metal, ended March 12, 2025. Mexico is not on the Section 338 list. Mexican scrap, the largest Mexican aluminum export to the U.S., is Free. Mexico shipped $1.81B in 2025.

faqs.question: Does USMCA exempt aluminum from the Section 232 tariff?
faqs.answer: No. U.S. note 16(b) to Chapter 99 says the Section 232 duty is collected in addition to any FTA or USMCA special rate, so USMCA-qualifying Canadian and Mexican aluminum pays 50% (or 25%). A USMCA claim still removes the base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty on the 12 non-Section 232 lines (powders, tanks, pot scourers, fasteners, wire cloth). It does not remove the Section 338 duty on Canadian extrusions and tubes.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on aluminum from China?
searchedAs: what is the tariff on aluminum from china to usa
faqs.answer: 75% to 81% on Chinese aluminum ingot, sheet, extrusions, wire and tubes: 50% Section 232 plus 25% Section 301 (U.S. note 31, heading 9903.91.01, since September 27, 2024) plus the base rate. Capacitor, cut-to-shape and backed foil and doors and windows are on List 4A at 7.5% instead (about 58% to 63%). Chinese cookware pays 28% to 36%, Chinese scrap 25%. Many Chinese aluminum products also carry antidumping and countervailing duties: extrusions, foil, common alloy sheet, wire and cable, lithographic plates and disposable containers.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on UK aluminum?
faqs.answer: 25% (heading 9903.82.04), or 15% on derivative articles (9903.82.05), when at least 95% of the aluminum was smelted or most recently cast in the United Kingdom; otherwise the standard 50% or 25%. The UK kept 25% when other countries went to 50% on June 4, 2025; the further arrangements contemplated by Executive Order 14309 have not been set up.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on Russian aluminum?
faqs.answer: 200% under Section 232 (9903.85.67 / 9903.85.68), on top of the column 2 rate (or 70% in its place on most aluminum subheadings) and a 12.5% Section 301 duty. The 200% also applies to aluminum of any other country if any of its primary aluminum was smelted in Russia or it was cast in Russia (note 19(m)), which is why the AIM license asks for the smelt and cast countries.

faqs.question: What are aluminum tariffs by country?
faqs.answer: For aluminum mill products: 50% plus the base rate from the UAE, India, the EU, Thailand and every other country, and 50% flat from FTA partners with a Free base rate (Canada, Mexico, Korea, Bahrain, Colombia); 100% for Canadian extrusions and tubes; 75% to 81% for China; 25% for UK aluminum with UK-smelted or cast metal; 200% or more for Russian metal. Differences show up on scrap and the non-Section 232 lines, and in company-specific AD/CVD duties.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import aluminum from?
searchedAs: where does the us import aluminum from
how much aluminum does the us import
faqs.answer: In 2025 the United States imported $26.47B of Chapter 76 aluminum. The largest suppliers were Canada ($9.69B), China ($1.97B), Mexico ($1.81B), the United Arab Emirates ($1.61B) and South Korea ($1.23B). The biggest product groups were unwrought aluminum (7601, $9.94B), plate, sheet and strip (7606, $3.83B) and structures, doors and windows (7610, $2.24B).

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on aluminum scrap?
faqs.answer: For almost every country, no. Aluminum waste and scrap (7602) is Free, is not on the Section 232 lists, and is on the general exemption list of the 2026 Section 301 actions (note 52(b)). Only Chinese scrap (25%, Section 301 List 3), Brazilian scrap (25%, Brazil Section 301) and Russian scrap pay extra. U.S. scrap imports rose 61.7% in 2025 to $2.16B.

faqs.question: Are there exemptions or exclusions from the aluminum tariffs?
faqs.answer: Very few. Proclamation 10895 ended all country exemptions and quotas and stopped new product exclusions on March 12, 2025. What remains: the UK rate (25% or 15%), the 10% rate for derivatives made with U.S.-smelted aluminum, Commerce-authorized Canadian and Mexican quantities at 25% (9903.82.19), the coming half-rate quota for companies building U.S. smelters (Proclamation 11045), and goods not on the note 16(c) lists (scrap, powders, tanks, most fasteners, wire cloth). Section 232 drawback is limited to clause 13 of Proclamation 11021.

faqs.question: How are aluminum tariffs calculated?
searchedAs: how are steel and aluminum tariffs calculated
faqs.answer: Add the base rate of the Chapter 76 line and the Section 232 rate (50% or 25%, UK 25% or 15%) applied to the full customs value, regardless of aluminum content since April 6, 2026, plus any other Chapter 99 duty that stacks: Section 301 for China, Section 338 for Canadian extrusions and tubes, or the Russia rates. The 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties do not stack on Section 232 aluminum. CBP's CSMS # 68253075 says to report the 9903.82 heading with the Chapter 76 number. AD/CVD cash deposits come on top.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for aluminum?
faqs.answer: Aluminum is HTS Chapter 76: unwrought ingot and billet 7601, scrap 7602, powders 7603, bars, rods and extruded profiles 7604, wire 7605, plate, sheet and strip 7606, foil 7607, tubes and pipes 7608, fittings 7609, structures, doors and windows 7610, cans and containers 7612, gas cylinders 7613, stranded cable 7614, cookware and household articles 7615, and other articles (castings, forgings, fasteners, ladders) 7616. Use the rate table to search by product name.
